youtube_title: Duplicate Execution in At-Least-Once Delivery | CS 5254 Week 10
summary: A worker finishes a job, but its acknowledgement is lost before the queue records success, so the same message runs again.
youtube_description:
A worker finishes a job, but its acknowledgement is lost before the queue records success, so the same message runs again. The lecture shows why duplicate execution is a design pressure, not a queue bug, and how to defend the invariant with evidence.

This CS 5254 Week 10 lecture explores duplicate execution and its impact on concurrent system design.
